analysis: Examined both changed files. StartCommand+Modes.swift head 216-217: runForeground now calls attachWeightHashes(to:verifiedWeightHashesFile: VerifiedWeightHashStore.path()), apparently adding a persisted on-disk cache of previously verified weight hashes. This is security-relevant to T-012/T-027/A-004 (operator replaces weights under ~/.cache/huggingface) and to T-041's binding of the SSD prefix cache to the verified weightHash in coordinator mode. If the store is keyed only by path/size/mtime, or is operator-writable and trusted without integrity protection, an operator (ADV-001) could swap weights while the attested binary keeps advertising the old hash, and stale weightHash would also mis-bind KV cache entries. The implementation of VerifiedWeightHashStore and the new attachWeightHashes parameter is not in this batch, so no regression is proven. Integration must check: store location and permissions, the invalidation key (content hash versus metadata), whether the entries are authenticated (e.g. with a KEK-derived MAC), the behavior on a corrupt or tampered store, and whether the cached hash flows into modelHashes, modelHashFingerprints, autopilotInventory and registration. The routing gate is in head 219-221. StartCommand.swift head 173-179: adds an informational GLMWiredLimitAdvice.startNotice warning. It computes advertisedModels with --model/--all overrides before the mode split, only to print the warning. Its output does not feed serving selection; runForeground still applies pinned selection separately. No security impact was identified beyond reading live wired-memory limits. The base/head of runLocalStandalone, the scheduled-window loop, the auto-update flow and the local-endpoint auth path are otherwise unchanged.
